title: Any Phone Becomes a TV Drawing Tablet | vitalii.no
description:
My kids wanted to draw with a real graphics tablet and see it on the big screen instead of squinting at a phone. The problem: a graphics tablet plugged into an Android phone had no way to send pen strokes to the browser running on the TV in another room, in real time.

I built a phone-side page that captures the tablet's pointer events at full pressure and rate, and a TV-side canvas that mirrors those strokes with its own toolbar, paper and a save button. The two sides connect directly over WebRTC, paired through a small Cloudflare Worker with a Durable Object room: a phone on the home network gets an auto-token, any other phone pairs with a 4-digit code, and if the direct link cannot establish, the same Durable Object relays the strokes instead so drawing keeps working either way.

The result: a phone with a $30 drawing tablet plugged in now works as a real TV canvas — no phone-screen squinting, no separate drawing app, and finished drawings save straight to cloud storage.
